grade_lead: Pick a school year and each date below is labelled with the year your child will be in at that time. The year you pick is the one for FY2026. This is simple arithmetic on the published dates — the city’s plan does not treat school years differently — and which school a child attends is decided by address.
meta_desc_schedule: A summary of the reorganization plan schedule, including briefings, opinion exchanges, and planned implementation dates.
notice: ⚠️ This is an unofficial community site and is not the official Komaki City website. For official information, please visit the Komaki City Board of Education.
phase1_body: Held "School Discussion Meetings" (5 sessions total), reported to community councils and neighborhood association heads. Shared the current situation in Shinooka district (rapid decline in student numbers, aging facilities) with local residents.
phase2_body: Conducted student surveys (online), parent surveys (online), Shiroyama 3&4-chome briefings, parent opinion exchange meetings (3 sessions), and a community briefing. Also conducted the new school name survey.
phase3_body: Held public comment on the draft reorganization plan. A total of 55 submissions were received (39 email, 13 fax, 1 mail, 2 in person). The city published responses and a revised plan.
phase4_body: Held the School District Advisory Committee on January 13, 2026. The 5th "School Discussion Meeting" was held on February 7 at the East Community Center.
phase5_body: Official decision on the reorganization plan, formulation of school bus plan, establishment of preparation committees for new schools, etc. Please check the official announcements from Komaki City Board of Education for details.
phase6_body: The 4-school system of Tokadai Higashi Elementary, Tokadai Nishi Elementary, Tokadai Higashi JHS, and Tokadai Nishi JHS will launch. School bus service for elementary students (fully funded by the city — free) will also begin.

Topic: Issues surrounding school education in Shinooka district
sched_desc10: 1st Parent Opinion Exchange Meeting (East Community Center)
sched_desc11: 2nd & 3rd Parent Opinion Exchange Meetings (East Community Center)
sched_desc15:
Public Comment Period
55 submissions received (39 email, 13 fax, 1 mail, 2 in person). City published responses and revised plan.
sched_desc18: School District Advisory Committee (Komaki City Hall East Building)
sched_desc19:
5th "Shinooka District School Discussion Meeting" (East Community Center Hall)
Topic: Draft reorganization plan for Shinooka district
sched_desc2:
2nd "Shinooka District School Discussion Meeting" (East Community Center Hall)
Topic: Review of 1st meeting, draft reorganization plan for Shinooka district
sched_desc20:
Plan Finalization & Implementation Preparation (in progress)
Establishment of preparation committees for Shinooka Gakuen's 4 schools, formulation of school bus plan, etc. For the latest information, check the official city page.
sched_desc21:
Shinooka Gakuen School Emblem Design Contest
Design a shared emblem for all 4 schools. Open to: Komaki city residents/students/workers, or those with school experience in Shinooka district. Prizes: ¥20,000 (1st) and ¥5,000 (runners-up) in Komaki Premium vouchers. Submit via web or paper form.
sched_desc22:
Parent/Guardian Briefing (Toryou JHS Gymnasium)
For: Parents of Toryou JHS district (including preschool children entering FY2027). No pre-registration needed. Approx. 2 hours. 28 people attended.
sched_desc23:
Parent/Guardian Briefing (Shinooka JHS Gymnasium)
For: Parents of Shinooka JHS district (including preschool children entering FY2027). No pre-registration needed. 73 people attended.
sched_desc24:
Parent/Guardian Briefing (Sue Elementary Gymnasium)
For: Parents of Sue Elementary district (including preschool children entering FY2027). No pre-registration needed. 66 people attended.
sched_desc25:
Parent/Guardian Briefing (Oshiro Elementary Gymnasium)
For: Parents of Oshiro Elementary district (including preschool children entering FY2027). No pre-registration needed. 104 people attended.
sched_desc26:
Parent/Guardian Briefing (Hikarigaoka JHS Gymnasium)
For: Parents of Hikarigaoka JHS district (including preschool children entering FY2027). No pre-registration needed. 67 people attended.
sched_desc27:
Parent/Guardian Briefing (East Community Center Hall)
For: All school district parents and local residents (covering both Tokadai Higashi & Nishi schools). No pre-registration needed. Approx. 2 hours. Limited parking — public transport encouraged. 45 people attended.
sched_desc28:
Phase 1 Reorganization — Launch (Planned)
Shinooka Gakuen (Tokadai Higashi Elem, Tokadai Nishi Elem, Tokadai Higashi JHS, Tokadai Nishi JHS) 4-school system starts. School bus service for elementary students begins (fully funded by city — free).
sched_desc28__after:
Phase 1 Reorganization — Carried Out
Shinooka Gakuen (Tokadai Higashi Elem, Tokadai Nishi Elem, Tokadai Higashi JHS, Tokadai Nishi JHS) began as a four-school system. School bus service for elementary students also started (fully funded by the city — free).
sched_desc29:
Briefing Session Q&A and Responses Published
Records of Q&A from each venue, along with responses to questions submitted via opinion sheets, have been published on the city's official website.
sched_desc3:
3rd "Shinooka District School Discussion Meeting" (East Community Center Hall)
Topic: Review of 2nd meeting, school districts & school buses, future direction
sched_desc30:
Joint exchange event of the five elementary schools (Years 4–5)
Year 4 and Year 5 pupils of the five Shinooka elementary schools met by year group at the East Community Centre. After a short dance, time was set aside for everyone to mix.
sched_desc31:
School bus application period
The application form and a briefing invitation were sent to guardians of children inside the service area. The form must be returned whether or not a seat is wanted. At the briefing for applicants, the stops, the timetable and the “School Bus Use Guidelines” will be handed out and explained, and a consultation session is planned. See the school bus page for details.
sched_desc32:
Joint exchange event of the five elementary schools (all years)
Following July’s event for Years 4–5, a joint event for every year group is planned. Exchanges between particular schools and year groups are also to continue on a planned basis.
sched_desc33:
Contract signed with the school bus operator
Seven firms were invited; Aoi Kotsu Co., Ltd. won with ¥111,750,000 (excl. tax). The contract runs 8 June 2026 – 31 March 2030 and covers Komaki City. See the school bus page.
sched_desc34:
Pre-entry health check (2027 intake)
Held at the five current elementary schools.
sched_desc35:
School bus trial rides and app testing
Children ride the actual buses to check the routes, the stops and how easy boarding is. The app used to confirm boarding is to be trialled in the same period.
sched_desc36:
Joint school management council of the eight schools
The eight schools being reorganised are to hold a joint management council.
sched_desc37:
Enrolment briefing and pre-commute trial
The briefing is held at the two new elementary and two new junior high schools. A “pre-commute” exercise helps children get used to the journey.
sched_desc38:
Closing ceremonies (five elementary, three junior high) and moving of equipment
Each of the eight current schools holds a closing ceremony, and equipment is moved to the new schools.
sched_desc39:
“Arigato Oshiro-sho” (citizen-run)
At Oshiro Elementary School, which is closing, a festival market in the gym and baseball on the ground are planned, with food trucks. Committee members and volunteers are being recruited. This is organised by residents, not by the city or the school. See community efforts.
sched_desc4:
4th "Shinooka District School Discussion Meeting" (East Community Center Hall)
Topic: Review of 3rd meeting, parent opinion exchange & community briefing results, review of draft reorganization plan
sched_desc40:
New School District Music Festival (community council)
In the gym of Hikarigaoka Junior High School, an event to widen ties across the new school district through music and dance. Applications to perform closed on 30 August 2026. This is run by the music section of the Hikarigaoka elementary school district community council, not by the city. See community efforts.
sched_desc41:
The “Shinooka Gakuen” emblem was decided
A single emblem for the four schools was chosen from 212 entries. The three ideals are drawn as a mathematical trefoil knot which, with a circle, forms a peach; an “S” sits at the centre, with a book and wings below. It will now be displayed at the schools and made into the school flag.
